items.topic: pi model not found: proxy provider needs models.json, not providers.json
items.claim: Adding provider 'proxy' (baseUrl, apiKey, api openai-responses) to ~/.pi/agent/providers.json is enough; pi would auto-discover models from /v1/models
items.fact: pi does not discover models from the proxy /v1/models. 'Error: Model "proxy/cc/claude-opus-5-5" not found' occurs. Models must be declared in ~/.pi/agent/models.json (providers.<name>.{baseUrl,api,apiKey,models:[{id,name,input,contextWindow,maxOutput,reasoning}]}); providers.json is not the model catalog. After declaring, `pi --list-models` shows proxy cc/claude-opus-5-5 and the model works. Bake models.json into the Docker image (COPY agent/models.json /home/pi/.pi/agent/models.json). Minimal model entry per pi docs is {"id":...}, but that alone did not fix it in providers.json.

items.topic: Diagnosing pi REGISTER_TIMEOUT in pi-dashboard container
items.claim: Spawned sessions fail with REGISTER_TIMEOUT 'Pi session started but never registered (timeout 30000ms)' (spawn-failures.log)
items.fact: Root cause is the pi child exiting code=1 (keeper log: 'pi exited code=1 elapsed=5s') because the model was unresolved. Keeper logs have 'pi output capture: disabled', so reproduce by running `node /app/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/cli.js --model <m> -p 'say hi'` inside the container to see the real error. Keeper logs: /home/pi/.pi/dashboard/sessions/keeper-<id>.log.

items.topic: Bash: UID is a readonly variable
items.claim: Using UID=... as shell var for Keycloak user id in a script
items.fact: In bash/zsh UID is readonly (set to 501); assignment fails silently and later API calls hit the wrong id (set password HTTP 404). Use another variable name (RID).

items.topic: Keycloak realm import only runs on first boot
items.fact: Keycloak imports the realm file only on first start. To add a user to a running instance use the admin API: get admin token (master realm, admin-cli), POST /admin/realms/pi-identity/users (201), then PUT /users/<id>/reset-password; or `docker compose down -v` for a fresh import. Also update realm file for rebuilds.

items.topic: Keycloak 'Invalid redirect URI' for LAN access
items.fact: When pi-dashboard is accessed via LAN IP (http://192.168.10.219:8010) the identity-login plugin redirects to <origin>/identity-login/callback, so Keycloak client dashboard-web (public, PKCE S256) must list the LAN/tailscale origins in redirectUris (e.g. http://192.168.10.219:8010/*, http://100.74.191.63:8010/*) both in realm file and live via admin API. Operator reported 'says invalida redirectory!'.

items.topic: pi-dashboard identity plane over LAN: issuer must be reachable by browser and container
items.claim: Keycloak forwarded only on localhost:18080 with issuer http://localhost:18080
items.fact: For LAN use, bind Keycloak to 0.0.0.0:18080, set PI_LOGIN_ISSUER and PI_LOGIN_BROWSER_ISSUER to the shared LAN issuer http://<LAN-IP>:18080/realms/pi-identity (no localhost forward in wrapper-entrypoint), so token issuer matches. Issuer depends on DHCP IP; if IP changes, rebuild/re-up. Plain HTTP, macOS firewall was off. Mac LAN IP en0 192.168.10.219, tailscale 100.74.191.63.

items.topic: pi-dashboard per-user session isolation via principalOwner
items.fact: With identity plane enforced, a session spawned with a user's Keycloak bearer (ROPC grant, client dashboard-web) is stamped principalOwner {iss, sub}; sessions list shows only own; accessing another user's session returns 404 (hidden), not 403. Spawn via POST to dashboard API with bearer. Observed odd 403 on own session was a test artifact (unexpanded variable).

items.topic: Review website: per-user decisions view and merge with conflicts
items.fact: Operator: all users should see their own accepted/declined version, and have a merge button that merges decisions into the main site, updating all users' states but showing conflicts on decisions. Operator chose to implement on review website (target/review-app, port 8791): each person opens with ?user=<name>, decisions in per-user store, own accepted/declined view, Merge folds into shared state and flags items where users chose differently as conflicts.
